title: Bound for real integrals supported on a compact set
statement: Use $\mathbf R$ [def-weil-field]. Let $X$ be a topological space with a sigma-algebra and a measure $\mu$ finite on compact subsets, meaning $\mu(K)<\infty$ for every compact $K\subseteq X$. Let $K\subseteq X$ be compact, $h:X\to\mathbf R$ a function with $h(x)=0$ for $x\notin K$, and $C\geq0$ a real number with $|h(x)|\leq C$ for $x\in K$. Then $\mu(K)<\infty$ and $$\left|\int_X h\,d\mu\right|\leq C\,\mu(K).$$ Here $\mu(K)$ on the right is its finite real value. The integral is the Bochner integral, assigned zero when the function is not integrable. No continuity or integrability hypothesis on $h$ is required. In particular this applies to Euclidean Lebesgue measure on $\mathbf R^m$ for every $m\geq0$.
